profile.name: Nisarg Shah
profile.description: Building data-driven solutions through statistical analysis, machine learning, and large-scale data processing, while exploring cloud, MLOps, and AI engineering.

featuredProjects.title: Uniswap V3 LP Position Profitability Prediction
featuredProjects.description: What happens when you open a concentrated liquidity position on Uniswap V3 — will it actually make money? This model predicts exactly that at the moment of opening, giving liquidity providers data-driven guidance on where to set their price range. Trained on 62,250 closed positions pulled from 9 on-chain data sources across the highest-volume pools, with custom features for tick ranges, fee events, and partial withdrawals. Logistic Regression and XGBoost were evaluated using chronological splits to avoid temporal leakage, and SHAP revealed the headline insight: positions whose price range didn't overlap the pool's recently traded range were profitable just 23% of the time — versus 60% when they did.

featuredProjects.title: Criteo CTR Prediction
featuredProjects.description: Same click-through-rate prediction, three very different computing setups — which one actually wins? The Criteo 1M dataset was preprocessed with median imputation, log transforms, feature hashing for high-cardinality categoricals, and sparse feature assembly, then fed into Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient-Boosted Trees models with 2-fold cross-validation. The best model hit 0.537 PR-AUC against a 25.5% positive-class baseline — but the real story was the benchmark: identical workflow run across a Docker-based PySpark cluster, an AWS EC2 Spark cluster, and single-machine scikit-learn, comparing how the same pipeline scales from laptop to cloud.

featuredProjects.title: Debunking the Left-Right Batting Advantage
featuredProjects.description: Contributed to an independent-study analysis of whether left-right batting partnerships are inherently better in international Test cricket. The heart of the study is a strike-change analysis: for every delivery where the strike had changed on the previous ball, the outcome (runs scored, dismissal) on that exact delivery is compared across left-left, right-right, and left-right pairings — spanning 750+ matches, 200,000+ strike changes, 100,000+ runs, and nearly 4,000 dismissals. The same strike-change comparison is repeated using only the top seven partnerships per match to limit lower-order noise. Supporting analyses compare partnership batting averages, total runs, and strike rates across all combinations. Because player names differed between the ball-by-ball and batting-hand datasets, the team joined them with a fuzzy matching algorithm that reached 96% accuracy. In every view — plain comparisons and strike-change alike — the differences between left-right and same-handed combinations were too small to establish a meaningful advantage.

allProjects.title: Navicore
allProjects.description: A multimodal, GPS-style route finder for Mumbai's transport network: it models the city's suburban rail, bus, metro and road networks as a single weighted graph built from stops, routes, and schedule data, then runs shortest-path search to surface the best rail + bus route between any two landmarks. Built in Python with NetworkX and shipped through an interactive live Streamlit deployment, it allows you to find the best path based on preference - Earliest Arrival, Least Interchange, Public Transport Only, Specific Mode of Transport.

allProjects.title: IPL Fantasy League Dashboard
allProjects.description: Automates the boring part of a fantasy cricket league: it scrapes live match data as games unfold, converts every player's performance into fantasy points using a role-based scoring rulebook, and drops everything into a polished dashboard — track the live leaderboard and points race, drill into your squad's individual contributions and boosters, review captain and vice-captain picks, dive into any match or player for a full breakdown, and catch live scores as they happen. Standings refresh automatically as each match progresses — no manual point tallying, no spreadsheets.

allProjects.title: PAT.ai: Data Analysis Assistant
allProjects.description: Wish you could explore a dataset without writing pandas code? PAT.ai is a Streamlit-based data analysis assistant that turns plain-English questions into real analytics. Type something like 'how does revenue vary by region?', and the app maps your query to a predefined analytical workflow, runs the statistical analysis quietly in the background, and returns a clean Plotly chart. It's a fast, conversational on-ramp to exploratory data analysis for anyone who wants answers, not syntax.
